overview: The Cigna Group is a Bloomfield, Connecticut-based health services company operating through two segments: Evernorth Health Services (pharmacy benefit management via Express Scripts, specialty pharmacy via Accredo, and care/health solutions) and Cigna Healthcare (U.S. employer-sponsored medical plans, international health, and supplemental benefits). Following the March 2025 sale of its Medicare Advantage and CareAllies businesses to Health Care Service Corporation (HCSC), Cigna is increasingly weighted toward Evernorth's pharmacy/PBM and specialty-drug distribution economics rather than traditional risk-based health insurance. It generated roughly $275 billion of revenue in FY2025 and operates primarily in the U.S., with a smaller international health book.

business_model.summary: Cigna earns money two ways: (1) Evernorth, which is now the larger profit engine, makes money on pharmacy benefit management spread/service fees, specialty pharmacy dispensing (Accredo), and care solutions sold largely to health plans, employers and government payers (including a multi-year services agreement with HCSC on the divested Medicare book); and (2) Cigna Healthcare, which underwrites and administers employer-sponsored (largely self-funded/ASO) medical, dental, behavioral and supplemental benefit plans domestically and health coverage for multinational/mobile employees internationally. Self-funded (administrative services only) employer business carries low insurance risk and steady fee income, while a shrinking book of fully-insured and individual plans carries underwriting risk.

revenue_streams.name: Evernorth Health Services (PBM, specialty pharmacy, care solutions)

business_model.customer_type: Predominantly B2B/B2B2C: large and mid-size employers, health plans, unions, government agencies, and other payers, distributed through brokers/consultants; individual and family plan (B2C) exposure is being wound down (exit announced for Jan 1, 2027)
business_model.geographic_mix: United States >90% of revenue; International Health serves globally mobile individuals and multinational employers in more than 200 countries/jurisdictions but is a small share of total revenue

competitive_position.market_position: Evernorth's Express Scripts is one of the 'Big Three' PBMs (with CVS Caremark and UnitedHealth's Optum Rx) controlling roughly 80% of U.S. prescription claims; Cigna Healthcare is a top-tier national commercial health plan but has exited Medicare Advantage and is exiting ACA individual plans, narrowing its health-plan footprint relative to UnitedHealthcare, Elevance and Aetna.

moat_factors.description: Express Scripts/Accredo scale gives negotiating leverage with manufacturers and pharmacies, and specialty drug distribution (including GLP-1s) is a high-growth, high-touch niche competitors struggle to replicate quickly
Multi-year embedded relationships with large self-funded employers and other health plans (including a transition services agreement with HCSC) create switching costs and revenue visibility
Longstanding broker/consultant relationships and multinational health network for globally mobile employees are difficult for new entrants to match
Complex compliance, network contracting, and data infrastructure requirements limit new PBM/insurer entrants, though ~60 smaller PBMs still compete on price

weaknesses: Loss of Medicare Advantage scale (sold to HCSC) removes a growth vector other national payers are pursuing
Exiting ACA Individual & Family Plans (369,000 members) shrinks the individual/B2C footprint
PBM business model under direct legislative and regulatory attack (delinking, spread-pricing bans) with uncertain multi-year economics
Heavy reliance on the 'Big Three' PBM oligopoly structure, which is now the target of federal and state scrutiny (including the FTC's 2026 settlement with Express Scripts)
Less diversified than UnitedHealth (no comparable Optum Health/care-delivery arm) or CVS (no retail pharmacy footprint)

growth_drivers: Evernorth's shift to a rebate-free, cost-plus PBM pricing model (fully insured plans starting 2027, standard for all clients by 2028) intended to pre-empt legislative delinking mandates and rebuild trust with plan sponsors

Specialty pharmacy and GLP-1/weight-management growth: EncircleRx, EnReachRx and EnGuide programs, plus the ~$3.5 billion investment in the former Walgreens-owned specialty pharmacy (Shields Health Solutions) and a $100 million AI-powered specialty pharmacy investment through 2028
Continued growth in self-funded/ASO employer medical enrollment and behavioral health/dental cross-sell
International Health expansion serving multinational and globally mobile employee populations
Capital redeployment from the ~$4.9 billion HCSC Medicare sale proceeds toward share repurchases and reinvestment in Evernorth

Portfolio simplification (Medicare exit completed 2025; ACA IFP exit effective 2027) intended to concentrate capital and management focus on higher-return, higher-growth segments ahead of the September 30, 2026 Investor Day where new multi-year targets are expected

business.description: Transition from rebate-based to cost-plus/flat-fee PBM pricing could compress near-term profitability even as it addresses regulatory risk; competitors (CVS TrueCost, Optum Rx cost-plus) are moving simultaneously, intensifying price competition
Exiting MA removes a large, growing government-program revenue base that peers (UnitedHealth, Humana, Elevance, CVS/Aetna) continue to scale
Discontinuing IFP plans in 11 states for 2027 requires an orderly member transition and could generate reputational/regulatory friction in affected states

business.risk: Customer concentration in large employer/PBM contracts
business.description: Loss or renegotiation of large self-funded employer or health-plan PBM contracts (including the HCSC transition services agreement) could be material to Evernorth revenue

financial.description: Debt/equity near 0.7-0.8x and net debt/EBITDA around 1.9x as of Q2 2026; manageable but a constraint on further large M&A or buyback pace if earnings soften

financial.risk: Margin volatility from pricing model transition
financial.description: Moving away from rebates could create a period of earnings-guidance uncertainty as new cost-plus arrangements are phased in through 2027-2028

regulatory.description: The Consolidated Appropriations Act reforms (effective 2028) will delink PBM compensation from Part D list prices/rebates, mandate full rebate pass-through, and restrict compensation to bona fide service fees — a structural change to PBM economics

February 2026 FTC settlement with Express Scripts (insulin pricing) requires eliminating spread pricing, decoupling compensation from list prices/rebates, relocating the Ascent GPO to the U.S., and ten years of FTC monitoring — a template for further scrutiny of Big Three PBMs

regulatory.risk: State-level ACA exchange and insurance regulation
regulatory.description: State regulators must approve the IFP exit in each of the 11 affected states, and future state mandates could affect commercial plan design and pricing
Ongoing Washington attention to drug pricing, PBM transparency, and health-plan practices creates a persistent overhang on sector valuations

macro.description: Medical care ratio (MCR) increased year over year in Q2 2026 (84.5% vs. 83.2%); unfavorable shifts in utilization or specialty drug cost trend directly compress underwriting margins

Rapid uptake of high-cost GLP-1/weight-management drugs raises plan sponsor cost pressure; Cigna is monetizing this via Evernorth programs but also bears utilization/benefit-design risk on the health-plan side
Modest direct exposure via investment portfolio yields on insurance reserves and cost of debt refinancing

execution.description: David Cordani (CEO for ~17 years) retired as CEO effective July 1, 2026, becoming Executive Chair; President/COO Brian Evanko (a 28-year Cigna veteran and former CFO) succeeded him — a long-planned, internal succession that reduces but does not eliminate transition risk

Simultaneously converting to a rebate-free/cost-plus pricing model, completing the ACA IFP exit, and integrating recent specialty pharmacy investments (Shields Health Solutions) represents significant concurrent operational change

macro_factors.industry_outlook: U.S. managed care and PBM industry faces structural change as regulators push to delink PBM compensation from drug list prices/rebates (effective 2028) and states/federal agencies scrutinize spread pricing; specialty pharmacy and GLP-1 management remain the fastest-growing sub-segment. Overall healthcare services demand remains a secular growth market (aging population, chronic disease management, specialty drug pipeline), but reimbursement and pricing model risk is elevated industry-wide.
macro_factors.cyclicality: Low-to-moderate - healthcare demand is largely non-discretionary and recession-resistant, though enrollment (especially individual exchange) can be sensitive to employment levels and government policy
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low - modest impact via investment income on insurance float and cost of debt
key_input_costs: Prescription drug costs (branded specialty and GLP-1 drugs)
Labor/wage costs for care management staff

recent_developments.event: Cigna scheduled an Investor Day for September 30, 2026 to present updated corporate strategy and financial targets; stock traded in the $268-$275 range in September 2026 amid broader managed-care sector weakness

Q2 2026 results: revenue rose 7% YoY to $71.7 billion; adjusted EPS of $7.78-$8.99 beat consensus; full-year adjusted EPS guidance raised to at least $30.45 (from $30.35); Cigna Healthcare MCR rose to 84.5% from 83.2% a year earlier
Evernorth announced a $100 million investment through 2028 in an AI-powered specialty pharmacy program
Brian Evanko formally became CEO, succeeding David Cordani, who moved to Executive Chairman

Cigna announced it will exit the ACA individual/family plan marketplace (on- and off-exchange) effective January 1, 2027, affecting approximately 369,000 members across 11 states, to focus capital on higher-growth/scalable businesses
Cigna announced CEO succession plan: David Cordani to retire effective July 1, 2026 and become Executive Chair; Brian Evanko (President & COO) to become CEO

FTC announced a settlement with Cigna's Express Scripts resolving an insulin-pricing lawsuit; Express Scripts agreed to eliminate spread pricing, decouple PBM compensation from list prices/rebates, relocate its Ascent GPO from Switzerland to the U.S., and accept 10 years of FTC monitoring
Q4/FY2025 results reported; FY2025 revenue of $274.9 billion (+11% YoY); FY2026 guidance established and dividend increased

Evernorth/Express Scripts announced a shift toward a rebate-free PBM pricing model, passing negotiated manufacturer discounts to patients at point of sale (fully insured clients starting 2027, standard for all clients by 2028), alongside a new cost-plus pharmacy reimbursement model beginning 2026
Evernorth announced a ~$3.5 billion investment in Shields Health Solutions, a specialty pharmacy platform formerly owned by Walgreens

Completed sale of Medicare Advantage, stand-alone Part D, Medicare Supplemental, and CareAllies businesses to Health Care Service Corporation (HCSC) for total consideration that rose to approximately $4.9 billion; proceeds directed primarily to share repurchases

items.notes: Up from prior guidance of at least $30.35; reflects Q1/Q2 2026 outperformance
Reaffirmed across FY2025 Q4 report and subsequent quarters
Raised from prior outlook of at least $4.5 billion, aided by favorable medical cost trend/utilization
Beat FactSet consensus of roughly $6.06-$7.50 depending on estimate basis; revenue of $71.7B, +7% YoY

items.target: Majority of HCSC sale proceeds (~$4.9B) directed to share repurchases
items.notes: Consistent with Cigna's historical capital return priority of buybacks plus a growing dividend

guidance.management_commentary: Management (CFO/COO Brian Evanko during Q1 2026 call, ahead of becoming CEO) framed the IFP exit and prior Medicare divestiture as deliberate portfolio simplification to concentrate investment in scalable, higher-return businesses (Evernorth specialty/PBM and core U.S. employer health). Management highlighted favorable medical cost trend and utilization versus assumptions as supporting the raised outlook, while flagging the multi-year transition to a rebate-free/cost-plus PBM model as a deliberate response to regulatory pressure that may create near-term earnings variability. The September 30, 2026 Investor Day is expected to lay out updated multi-year financial targets.

bull_case: Evernorth's scale in PBM and specialty pharmacy (Express Scripts, Accredo) positions Cigna to capture continued growth in specialty drugs and GLP-1 management, a structurally growing category

Portfolio simplification (Medicare Advantage exit, ACA IFP exit) concentrates capital in higher-return, more scalable businesses and funds substantial share buybacks from ~$4.9 billion in divestiture proceeds

Getting ahead of PBM regulatory risk via a voluntary shift to rebate-free/cost-plus pricing could rebuild trust with plan sponsors and pre-empt harsher mandated reforms, potentially preserving a competitive advantage over slower-moving peers

Valuation is undemanding versus history and peers (trailing P/E near 11x, forward P/E under 9x per info.json screen data) with raised FY2026 guidance and consensus analyst price targets implying meaningful upside from current levels (~$268-275)
Smooth, long-planned internal CEO succession (Evanko, a 28-year company veteran and former CFO) reduces strategic-drift risk versus an outside hire
bear_case: The PBM business model is under simultaneous attack from federal legislation (2028 delinking mandates), an FTC settlement requiring elimination of spread pricing and Express Scripts compensation reform, and competitive moves by CVS Caremark and Optum Rx to similar cost-plus models — multi-year earnings power of the core profit engine is genuinely uncertain

Exiting Medicare Advantage and ACA individual plans shrinks Cigna's addressable market in two of the fastest-growing segments of U.S. healthcare, ceding share to UnitedHealth, Humana, Elevance and CVS/Aetna

Rising medical cost ratios (84.5% in Q2 2026 vs. 83.2% a year earlier) signal utilization/cost trend pressure that could continue to compress underwriting margins in the remaining Cigna Healthcare book

Heavy reliance on the concentrated 'Big Three' PBM structure invites continued antitrust and political scrutiny that could impose further remedies or reputational damage beyond the Express Scripts insulin settlement

Execution risk is elevated with several major simultaneous transitions underway (PBM pricing model conversion, IFP exit, CEO transition, integration of the Shields Health Solutions investment) heading into a September 2026 Investor Day where new targets could disappoint if any workstream slips
